in_text_mentions: ement of the extremities ‒ particularly the legs ‒ while sparing the feet, resulting in a characteristic demarcation above the ankles. The so-called “cuffing sign” is a clinical hallmark of lipedema (Fig. 7). In contrast, lymphedema often begins in the distal extremities, involves the feet, and is commonly unilateral or asymmetrically bilateral. The presence of Stemmer’s sign (inability to pinch the skin on the dorsum of the toes) strongly suggests lymphedema but is absent in pure lipedema. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A anterior view of 44-year-old male explicitly captioned as stage II lipedema showing bilateral symmetrical thigh fat and ankle cuff with foot sparing, matching vocabulary findings. B: Panel B lateral view of same stage II lipedema patient showing thigh subcutaneous fat accumulation with ankle demarcation and foot sparing visible laterally. C: Panel C posterior view of same stage II lipedema patient showing bilateral symmetrical thigh/buttock fat accumulation with ankle cuff and foot sparing.
panels.attribution_text: Amato et al. Lipedema in Men: A Retrospective Case Series of Five Patients From a Brazilian Referral Center.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.87332. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Case 5: baseline anterior, lateral, and posterior views of a 44-year-old male with stage II lipedema (A) Anterior, (B) lateral, and (C) posterior photographs demonstrate bilateral, symmetrical subcutaneous fat accumulation predominating in the thighs and buttocks, with sharp demarcation above the ankles and sparing of the feet. Note the “wide legs” phenotype and relative preservation of lower-leg contour despite overall adipose excess. This patient had post-viral hypothyroidism on levothyroxine and a positive family history (sister), and these images were captured prior to initiation of the ketogenic diet and endocrine follow-up.
in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed stage II lipedema with bilateral fat accumulation in the lower extremities and notable capillary fragility (Figure 5). Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scan confirmed 38.5% total body fat with disproportionate distribution in the lower limbs. Adjusted BMI calculations and fat ratios supported the lipedema diagnosis.

in_text_mentions: The classification of stages including half stages are described below (Table 2) and presented as photos (Figure 1). As the number assigned to a stage increases, changes in skin texture become more extensive reflecting fibrosis of skin and tissue fibers [1] and fibrosis and greater amounts of glycosaminoglycans in the interstitial space [1,26] along with increased amounts of subcutaneous tissue and size of masses in the tissue.
